articles.title: Brain structure changes appear seven years before Alzheimer’s plaques are detected
articles.summary: New research indicates that changes in the brain's outer layer can be detected at least seven years before amyloid plaques reach high levels. This challenges the traditional timeline of how Alzheimer's disease develops.

articles.summary: arXiv:2609.28475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forecasting agents increasingly combine language-model reasoning, retrieval, ensembling, and calibration, but it remains unclear when each behavior should be trusted. articles.summary: arXiv:2609.28506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: TW3Cast is a time-series forecasting system that reaches position 3 of 130 entries on the GIFT-Eval benchmark by mean MASE rank, as of 2026-09-14. articles.title: PAWS: Policy-driven Agentic World Simulation
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.28547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy interventions propagate through public communication, institutional decisions, and stakeholder responses, yet datasets for financial multi-agent simulation rarely connect these processes to temporally aligned historical evidence. articles.title: More REM sleep linked to lower risk of 83 diseases
articles.summary: A large study tracking more than 95,000 people suggests that how you sleep may be linked to your risk of developing dozens of diseases. People who spent more time in REM sleep had lower risks of 83 conditions, including dementia, heart failure, and Parkinson’s disease, while more deep sleep was associated with lower risks of conditions such as type 2 diabetes and major depression.

articles.title: New eye-tracking study reveals how followers use gaze to show conscientiousness
articles.summary: New research shows that highly conscientious people strategically direct their gaze at leaders during workplace negotiations. This nonverbal behavior acts as a powerful signal, making them appear more reliable and diligent to their colleagues.

articles.summary: arXiv:2609.25013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tabular foundation models have recently shown strong potential for structured biomedical data analysis.
